ratings_why.fun: Defer plus 'biggest' lets any tribe's unit become the favourite, and seating for Windhover, Vane and Föhn is a real puzzle each turn.
ratings_why.distinct: Defer and a Gale that pays out in the shop are fresh, but extra out-of-turn attacks still read as a Windfury family at heart.

verdict_why: v2 fixed the Vane mirror, Lady's favourite and Föhn's Bristle wording; what is left is taste, not breakage.

points.text: Old Föhn is 2/11, so early he is often your biggest unit and every Defer turns into his own weak Gusts. Lean into it: a card or build line that wants the soaker to be the favourite.

Under Lady High Pressure the crown can move mid-fight when the favourite takes damage, and the whole Defer queue flips. Consider fixing the favourite at Start of Combat for readability, or show the crown on screen.
Master of the Wild Hunt's mass Gust at 20 makes Lady's Deferring courtiers swing for once; that reversal is a great hidden combo worth naming in Build A.
Red Sky at Night only turns Gale into gold; a small rider tied to who Gusted (say the favourite) would give it a seating decision.
Gale Warning on a Gust Page or the Couriers under Sir Vane stacks opening Gusts nicely; one more item reader would give the Warnings a second home.

standouts.why: Turns the whole board into one favourite's ammunition and makes 'who is biggest' the key decision.
A soaker that redirects return damage, including Bristle, and quietly competes for the crown himself.
One-sided seating rule that also chains off Gusts and Defer, so placement matters every turn.

weakest.why: Plain gold off a threshold; no decision once it is on the board.
Generic stats to your biggest unit; useful but one obvious job.
A Gale reader with no interaction beyond growing itself.

flags.note: With Wild Hunt doubling the Gale, the +2/+2 board-wide step at 10 is reached most fights.
Warnings keep the Gale at 8, which brings more Warnings; linear, but worth the runaway check.
Ties for biggest, and whether the exempt unit changes mid-fight, need a stated rule.
